extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduates / graduate students studying algebraic topology
extracted.subtask_description: Statements, constructions and technical lemmas in CW homotopy theory: excision for relative homotopy, constructions of spaces with prescribed homotopy, Hurewicz theorems and maps, plus construction, fibrations and the long exact sequence of homotopy groups, and illustrative examples (e.g. Hopf bundle, CP^∞).

rubrics_metrics.name: πn(S1 ∨ Sn) computation / non-finitely-generated example
rubrics_metrics.description: For the wedge S1 ∨ Sn one has πn(S1 ∨ Sn) ≈ Z[t, t^{-1}] (Laurent polynomials in t and t^{-1] with Z coefficients). This shows homotopy groups of a finite CW complex need not be finitely generated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as an example that contrasts finiteness properties of homology vs homotopy; illustrates nontrivial π1-action giving infinite generation. See Exercise referenced for further failure cases (e.g. π3(S1 ∨ S2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Serre finiteness criterion (informal mention)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a space has trivial action of π1 on all πn's, then Serre's theorem says the homotopy groups of such a space are finitely generated iff the homology groups are finitely generated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentioned as a remedy to the non-finite-generation pathology when the π1-action is trivial; proof reference given ([SSAT]).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 4.28: relative homotopy vs quotient (excision range)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a CW pair (X,A) is r-connected and A is s-connected, with r,s ≥ 0, then the quotient map X→X/A induces πi(X,A)→πi(X/A) which is an isomorphism for i ≤ r+s and a surjection for i = r+s+1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses attaching a cone CA to X, contractibility of CA, homotopy equivalence X∪CA → X/A, and excision for the pair (CA,A) because (CA,A) is (s+1)-connected. This is a tool for computations where collapsing A simplifies the space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example 4.29: realizing πn by attaching (n+1)-cells
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is obtained from a wedge of S^n's (n≥2) by attaching (n+1)-cells via basepoint-preserving maps ϕβ: S^n → (wedge), then πi(X)=0 for i<n and πn(X) is the quotient of the free abelian group πn(wedge) by the subgroup generated by the attaching classes [ϕβ].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any subgroup can be realized this way by choosing attaching maps representing a set of generators; thus every abelian group can be realized as πn(X) for such a CW complex. This is the higher-dimensional analogue of constructing 2D CW complexes with prescribed π1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition / construction of Eilenberg–MacLane spaces K(G,n)
rubrics_metrics.description: A space X with exactly one nontrivial homotopy group πn(X) ≈ G is called K(G,n). For n>1 assume G abelian. Construct by building an (n−1)-connected CW complex of dimension n+1 with πn ≈ G and then attach higher-dimensional cells to kill πi for i>n without affecting πn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SP(S^n) (infinite symmetric product) gives K(Z,n); more generally SP(M(G,n)) gives K(G,n). Products of K(G,n)'s realize arbitrary sequences of groups as homotopy groups of a space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 4.30: uniqueness of K(G,n)
rubrics_metrics.description: The homotopy type of a CW complex K(G,n) is uniquely determined by G and n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses Lemma 4.31: given X (wedge of S^n plus (n+1)-cells) and any homomorphism ψ:πn(X)→πn(Y) with Y path-connected, one can construct f:X→Y with f_* = ψ, and then extend inductively over higher cells to a homotopy equivalence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 4.31: realising maps on πn by maps of CW complexes
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a CW complex built from a wedge of S^n's by attaching (n+1)-cells (for n≥1), then for every homomorphism ψ:πn(X)→πn(Y) with Y path-connected there exists a map f:X→Y with f_* = ψ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct f on the wedge by sending each sphere by a map representing ψ([i_α]) and extend over (n+1)-cells because the images of attaching maps are nullhomotopic in Y (their classes map to 0 under ψ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 4.32: (simple) Hurewicz theorem
rubrics_metrics.description: If a space X is (n−1)-connected with n≥2 then Hi(X)=0 for i<n and πn(X) ≈ Hn(X). For a pair (X,A) that is (n−1)-connected with A simply-connected and nonempty, Hi(X,A)=0 for i<n and πn(X,A)≈Hn(X,A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof reduces to CW complexes with no cells below dimension n and at most n+1 cells; πn computed as cokernel of the boundary map in homotopy which equals the cellular boundary in homology, giving the isomorphism. Use Proposition 4.28 for relative reduction to quotient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 4.33: homology isomorphism implies homotopy equivalence (simply-connected case)
rubrics_metrics.description: A map f:X→Y between simply-connected CW complexes is a homotopy equivalence if f_*:Hn(X)→Hn(Y) is an isomorphism for each n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: take mapping cylinder Mf and use relative Hurewicz to show πn(Mf,X)=0 for all n, so inclusion induces isomorphisms on all homotopy groups and hence is a homotopy equivalence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example 4.35: homology isomorphism need not imply homotopy isomorphism when π1 acts nontrivially
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct X=(S^1 ∨ S^n) ∪ e^{n+1} (n>1) by attaching e^{n+1} via a map representing 2t−1 ∈ Z[t,t^{-1}] so that inclusion S^1 → X induces isomorphism on all homology groups and on πi for i<n, but not on πn: πn(X) ≈ Z[t,t^{-1}]/(2t−1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This example demonstrates the essential role of the simple-connectivity (or trivial π1-action) hypothesis in results like Corollary 4.33 and the Hurewicz theorem: nontrivial π1-action can kill the correspondence between homology and homotopy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and properties of the Hurewicz map
rubrics_metrics.description: Hurewicz map h:πn(X,A,x0)→Hn(X,A) defined by h([f])=f_*(α) where α is generator of Hn(Dn,∂Dn) (or for absolute case use S^n). For n>1 this map is a homomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 4.36 proves additivity: for maps f,g:(Dn,∂Dn)→(X,A), (f+g)_* = f_* + g_* using wedge and collapse arguments; naturality and compatibility with homotopies noted. Kernel contains elements of form [γ][f]−[f] coming from nontrivial π1-action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 4.36: Hurewicz map is a homomorphism (n>1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For n>1, the Hurewicz map h:πn(X,A,x0)→Hn(X,A) is a group homomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses the map c: D^n→D^n ∨ D^n collapsing equator and quotient maps q1,q2 to reduce to additivity of induced homology maps, which holds for any homology theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of π'_n and general Hurewicz theorem (Theorem 4.37)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define π'_n(X,A,x0) as πn(X,A,x0) modulo subgroup generated by elements [γ][f]−[f] (or normal subgroup when n=2). Theorem 4.37: If (X,A) is (n−1)-connected pair of path-connected spaces with n≥2 and A≠∅ then h':π'_n(X,A,x0)→Hn(X,A) is an isomorphism and Hi(X,A)=0 for i<n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This general form accounts for nontrivial π1-actions by passing to the quotient π'_n; proof involves cellular arguments, Lemma 4.38 and a diagram chase analogous to the five-lemma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 4.38: relative πn for attaching n-cells is free π1-module (n≥3 case)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a connected CW complex and cells e^n_α are attached (n≥2) to form W=X∪_α e^n_α, and inclusion π1(X)→π1(W) is an isomorphism, then πn(W,X) is a free π1(X)-module with basis the classes of the characteristic maps of the attached cells. In particular this always holds if n≥3. For n=2 the statement is that π2(W,X) is generated by the characteristic maps together with their images under the π1-action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses passage to universal covers: lifts of cells under deck transformations give free basis; n=2 case requires Whitehead's analysis (free crossed π1-module) and a reduction to 1-dimensional X.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 4.39: π'_2 is abelian
rubrics_metrics.description: For any (X,A,x0) the identity a + b − a = (∂a)b holds for all a,b∈π2(X,A,x0), where ∂:π2→π1 is the boundary; hence π'_2(X,A,x0) is abelian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The formula relates the nonabelian group operation in π2 to the π1-action; proof given by constructing a specific homotopy (pictures indicated). This lemma is used in establishing Hurewicz for n=2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 4.40: plus construction (simple case H1=0)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a connected CW complex with H1(X)=0 (i.e., π1(X) is perfect) then there exists a simply-connected CW complex X^+ and a map X→X^+ inducing isomorphisms on all homology groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct X' by attaching 2-cells along loops generating π1 to kill π1; then H2(X') splits as H2(X)⊕H2(X',X) and one represents basis of the free summand by maps S^2→X' and attach 3-cells to kill them, yielding X^+. This is the basic Quillen plus-construction idea used to kill perfect subgroups of π1 while preserving homology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quillen plus-construction (generalization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given X and a perfect subgroup H⊂π1(X) (the covering corresponding to H has π1≈H), one can form X^+ by gluing in the mapping cylinder Mp of the covering X̃→X and applying the previous construction to obtain X^+; the induced map π1(X)→π1(X^+) is surjective with kernel the normal subgroup generated by H, and X→X^+ induces homology isomorphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to 'abelianize' π1 in many applications (e.g., when G has perfect commutator subgroup), while preserving homology. Mapping-cylinder/gluing and van Kampen are the key tools; warns there are limits on which subgroups can be killed while preserving homology (e.g. π1=Z×Z case).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: homotopy lifting property and fibrations (Serre fibrations)
rubrics_metrics.description: A map p:E→B has the homotopy lifting property with respect to a space X if any homotopy g_t:X→B and a lift g_0 admitting a lift to E can be extended to a homotopy lifting g_t. A fibration is a map with the homotopy lifting property with respect to all spaces; having the property for disks D^k for all k≥0 (equivalently for CW pairs) is the Serre fibration condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This property is the correct topological analogue of exactness giving a long exact sequence of homotopy groups. Projection of a product B×F→B and covering maps are standard examples; Serre fibrations arise often and suffice to get the long exact sequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 4.41: relative isomorphism and long exact sequence for fibrations
rubrics_metrics.description: If p:E→B has the homotopy lifting property with respect to disks D^k for all k≥0, and choose basepoints b0∈B and x0∈F=p^{-1}(b0), then p_*:πn(E,F,x0)→πn(B,b0) is an isomorphism for all n≥1. Hence, for path-connected B there is a long exact sequence ...→πn(F,x0)→πn(E,x0)→πn(B,b0)→π_{n-1}(F,x0)→...→π0(E,x0)→0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof constructs lifts of maps In→B using relative homotopy lifting and shows surjectivity/injectivity of p_* by homotopy-extension and permutation of coordinates arguments. This is the technical core that produces the long exact sequence of a fibration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition / local triviality of a fiber bundle
rubrics_metrics.description: A fiber bundle F→E→B is a projection p:E→B such that each b∈B has neighborhood U with a homeomorphism h:p^{-1}(U)→U×F commuting with projection to U; h is a local trivialization and carries each fiber Fb homeomorphically to {b}×F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fiber bundles are locally products though not necessarily globally; examples: covering spaces (discrete fiber), Möbius band (interval fiber), projective-bundle S^1→S^{2n+1}→CP^n, Hopf bundle S^1→S^3→S^2. Local trivializations are given explicitly in the CP^n example (use coordinate charts Ui where z_i≠0).

rubrics_metrics.name: Example: Hopf bundle and projective bundle S^1→S^{2n+1}→CP^n
rubrics_metrics.description: For complex projective space CP^n, projection p:S^{2n+1}→CP^n (quotient by S^1 action) has fiber S^1; local trivializations hi on Ui = {[z]: z_i≠0} are given by hi(z) = ([z], z_i/|z_i|). The n=1 case yields the Hopf bundle S^1→S^3→S^2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compute homotopy groups via the long exact sequence of the fibration: e.g., π2(S^2) ≈ π1(S^1) and for i≥3 one gets πi(S^3)≈πi(S^2). The geometric picture (tori decomposition of S^3 into circle fibers) illustrates fiber geometry and monodromy.
